text:
Situation: Diazepam 10 mg tablets have been on FDA's shortage list since 2022-06-15, a span of 52 months as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 31 tablets (4.7 days on hand). Corvale General holds 142 tablets (18.3 days on hand). Both sites use NDC 76420031610 labeled by ASCLEMED USA INC., which identifies the plant as ASCLEMED USA INC. DBA ENOVACHEM (FEI 3001452204).

Why (FDA record): FDA inspected that plant on 2018-09-27 and classified it OAI, with the classification known on 2018-12-26. FDA's shortage listing for diazepam began 2022-06-15 and remains active.

Our position: Internal transfer is the only option that uses verified supply and avoids unverified vendors. Corvale General can spare 33 tablets while retaining two weeks of supply; Corvale East would reach 10 days on hand.

Recommended actions:
1. Execute transfer of 33 tablets of diazepam 10 mg from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires approval by pharmacy director and completion of a controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V).
2. Document the transfer in the inventory system and notify both site pharmacists — requires pharmacy director sign-off.

Not recommended: Purchasing from Advanced Rx Pharmacy of Tennessee, LLC; Advanced Rx of Tennessee, LLC; Aurobindo Pharma Limited; or Chartwell RX, LLC. None appear on FDA's shortage list today and their labels name no identifiable plant.
